scope: Time64 migration audit/policy only; no BE98 or BE19000AI executable modified and no clock set
policy: Use time64 by default in every new or rebuildable component. Keep a time32 compatibility boundary only when required by a demonstrated retained binary/protocol ABI and only after evaluating a proper source conversion, versioned interface or explicit adapter.

default_build_contract.arm64: 64-bit time_t is native. New tools/broker/services default arm64 and use fixed-width versioned IPC fields.
armel_armhf: Use _TIME_BITS=64 and _FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64 for normal newly built components, with sizeof(time_t)==8 and sizeof(off_t)==8 compile-time tests. Preserve required float ABI separately.
Verify compiler/dpkg-buildflags effective defaults rather than relying on GCC version alone.
Never apply -U_TIME_BITS/-U_FILE_OFFSET_BITS to every armel build just because old proprietary blobs exist.
Audit every public struct, pointer parameter, return value, callback, shared-memory region, wire record and persisted record shared with unchanged code.
default_build_contract.kernel: Image-v9 now implements ARM32 time64 syscalls and has physical armel/armhf glibc timer validation. Existing AIO remains disabled; legacy socket timestamps/ioctls are outside that syscall patch coverage.
default_build_contract.libc: Retain existing old symbol ABI for unchanged blobs while offering glibc time64 redirects to rebuilt code; upgrading libc does not rewrite old executable layouts or promote its time_t.

Select an explicit vendor protocol version, not the consumer CPU architecture. Recompute AI-specific layout and producer size; do not reuse BE98 byte counts.

If unchanged callers must keep rfctime, preserve its original ABI entry and expose a separate time64 API or tested wrapper for new callers. Range-check any conversion; do not relabel the existing symbol as a larger struct ABI.
be19000ai_concrete_boundaries.limit: Current stock pair both uses legacyABI and is not claimed broken; the conflict arises when replacing only one side.

be19000ai_concrete_boundaries.action: Rebuild available code against modern headers and verify actual redirects (__time64, __localtime64*, __stat64_time64 or statx as applicable). Keep legacy exports for untouched consumers. Audit callbacks and structs passed across library/object boundaries before mixing old and new TUs.
be19000ai_concrete_boundaries.limit: Name/version evidence identifies legacy calls; it does not establish all execution paths or all internal timestamp arithmetic.

be19000ai_concrete_boundaries.action: Recover compatible source or implement and test missing ABI/API behavior before a full time64 replacement. Keep isolated legacy component as explicit temporary boundary if unable to replace it; do not ship the incomplete rebuild just to claim time64.

component_migration_order.checks: No assertion that time64 kernel/libc changed old binary layout. Protocol round trips, range checks and failure semantics; do not wrap overflow back into negative epochs.

component_migration_order.checks: No hard/soft-float library mixing; sizeof/time64 syscalls and package ABI closure.

specific_porting_rules.timers: Use CLOCK_MONOTONIC for intervals/timeouts; real-time64 for wall clock. Convert kernel/library structs through declared APIs, not casts. Test >2038 timerfd/clock/IPC deadlines only in disposableVM; hardware probes must not set global clock.
specific_porting_rules.stat: Use rebuilt headers and time64 stat wrappers or explicit statx. A 32-bit object compiled with old struct stat cannot accept a new struct stat* solely because symbol resolution succeeds.
specific_porting_rules.shared_and_wire_structs: Define fixed-width fields, endianness and protocol version; assert complete byte layouts. Decode legacy fields into int64 application values, encode only with validated representability. Once both sides are upgradeable, migrate protocol/storage schema to64bits with explicit compatibility.
specific_porting_rules.callbacks: Audit callback typedefs and retained-object callsites. time_t parameters/returns may change ARM register allocation and alignment; function names and SONAME alone cannot validate them.
specific_porting_rules.format_and_parse: Replace %ld assumptions about time_t with explicit intmax_t/PRIdMAX casts or deliberate int64 formats; on32bit use strtoimax/strtoll plus bounds checks instead of atol/strtol for64bit epochs. Keep FORTIFY enabled and fix bounded buffers.
specific_porting_rules.persistent_data: Identify binary records, SQL schemas, NVRAM text epochs and public JSON representations. Use transactional/versioned migration and fixtures across2038; no blind cast or reinterpretation of old files.

legacy_exceptions_policy.historical_recipe_boundary: BE98 armel-multiarch early four-library compiler migration used -U_TIME_BITS/-U_FILE_OFFSET_BITS. That was a frozen ABI migration scope, not the policy for this new Ubuntu rootfs. Re-audit each package and use time64 unless an actual exported boundary requires a retained legacy form.

busybox_monotonic.config: release/src/router/busybox/config_base:124 CONFIG_MONOTONIC_SYSCALL=y; board-generated config still needs confirmation for the rebuilt package
busybox_monotonic.observed: get_mono(struct timespec*) at244-247 still passes libc struct directly to syscall(__NR_clock_gettime). monotonic_ns/us/ms/sec all call this helper.
busybox_monotonic.patch_behavior: When __USE_TIME_BITS64 is defined, use libc clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC,ts); otherwise retain the existing raw call. This fixes user/kernel structure translation and retains time64. Observed glibc2.44 defines __USE_TIME_BITS64 for native arm64 too, so the tested arm64 build also selects libc; legacy armel remains the tested raw branch.
busybox_monotonic.known_failure: BE98 rebuilt ARM32 had sizeof(time_t)=8,sizeof(timespec)=16,tv_nsec offset8; legacy syscall wrote only first8bytes and left sentinel bytes intact, corrupting ping RTT. The correction worked through libc even on old BE98 kernel with clock_gettime64 ENOSYS. Kernel9 new syscall support does not make the old syscall write a new larger struct.
busybox_monotonic.current_stock_boundary: Current AI BusyBox is still old glibc/time32 with legacy syscall import, so this is a required source fix before its time64 rebuild, not a claim of the current stock mismatch.
safe_port_steps: Apply the exact hash-bound hunk in a disposable package source copy; enable normal ARM32 time64/file-offset64 defaults rather than disabling them.
Build armel time64 and arm64 variants with unchanged relevant applets; assert time_t/timespec sizes and verify dynamic import/normal-loader closure against intended libc.

In QEMU #9 run the preserved sentinel/ABI probe, compare libc CLOCK_MONOTONIC and all monotonic helpers across successive samples; verify monotonic deltas and nanosecond range, bounded sleep/timeout and ping TTL deadline. No wall-clock change is required.

Test post2038 date formatting and sparse large files; before replacing BusyBox also test udhcpc scripts, syslog IPC, login/auth, hotplug and mount applets with their actual ASUS contracts. Prior arm64 candidate did not cover all these.

staged_implementation.integration: Separate userspace stack using scripts/apply-patch-stack.py conventions; kernel-only stack and current vendor source checkout are unchanged.
staged_implementation.runtime_limit: Focused actual helper functions under qemu-user/native host with explicitglibc2.44; not a full BusyBox rebuild or fresh physical acceptance.

cfg_shared_memory.observed: reportStartTime[] is still time_t; cm_isSlaveOnline(time_t) and cm_setReOffline(time_t*) are separate source-level callable contracts requiring retained-object audit.
cfg_shared_memory.safety: Textual patch compatibility is not a target layout test. Keep normal application time64; define the retained producer wire version independently from consumer architecture, then assert AI-specific total size/offsets/alignment against the actual producer fixture. Do not copy BE98 table byte counts or use __arm__ as the protocol selector for an arm64 reader.
safe_port_steps: Capture exact AI SDK feature macros and enumerate all CM_CLIENT_TABLE producers/readers plus any time-bearing by-value/pointer/callback boundary with retained objects.

Compile legacy layout fixture and modern armel/arm64 reader fixture; require every field offset and complete initialized-byte pattern to match the retained producer protocol. Inspect actual shared-memory segment size read-only before physical integration.

Use explicit int32 wire timestamp only for the retained32bit producer, convert to64bit internal time with checked encode/decode. Upgrade the producer/protocol to64bits when source-compatible; reject overflow rather than silently truncate.

Exercise empty/invalid shared-memory handling, AiMesh topology/client counts and interval calculations in QEMU fixtures, then actual HTTPD service on a controlled hardware trial without rebooting radios.

rfctime.implementation: rfctime(const time_t *timep,char *ts_string,int len) calls localtime_r(timep,&tm) and strftime.
rfctime.be98_examined_source: httpd-dashboard-fix-20260917/src/misc.c:7641 likewise keeps time_t*; no distinct rfctime64/__wrap_rfctime found in examined HTTPD/dashboard/AiMesh/platform source checkpoints. This is scoped search, not a claim about every historical file.
rfctime.actual_elf_edge: Current AI HTTPD imports rfctime; current AI libshared exports it. A time64 consumer with old library reads the wrong-width pointee, while a newtime64 library serving oldpointer callers could read beyond their4byte object.
safe_port_steps: Inventory every binary/object importing rfctime and its known compile ABI before changing exported signature.

Prefer a new explicit64bit API (for example timestamp int64_t by value) for rebuilt code, retain old rfctime entry with explicit legacy32bit pointee contract only for retained callers, or upgrade all source-visible callers together with distinct compatibility entrypoints. Do not cast time_t pointers.

Use separate legacy and modern caller fixtures with canaries, dates before/at/after2038 including2100, TZ/DST transitions, output-length boundaries and failure checks. Preserve FORTIFY; oldformat overflow must fail explicitly.
Run loader/relocation plus HTTPD authentication/cookie/date/log paths against final linked libraries. Source-level argument type changes alone do not prove mixed retained objects safe.

implementation_followup.result: The exact BE98 BusyBox fix is now staged as a board-pinned Ubuntu userspace patch, with old ARM32 failure reproduced and four passing ABI fixtures. AiMesh wire-field pattern still requires AI producer-layout validation; rfctime still requires a deliberate compatibility API implementation. No blanket time32 compilation and no live deployment.
